sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year, from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F145][F1][F8].
Net income grew only 0.4% a year and diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year; the share series has a basis break at the 2020 stock split [F147][F149][D76][P74].
FY2021 was the sharpest break, with operating margin down 14.6pp to 15.5%, the window low [D107][F20][D298].
FY2023 reversed it, with operating margin up 23.5pp to 41.3%, the window high [D177][F22][D299]; the cited filings do not explain that move.
FPL (other) supplied 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271] and 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth [D273][D236].
FY2025 FPL revenue rose 7.7% [D272], mainly on storm cost recovery of about $1.09 billion, partly offset by lower fuel recovery [P18][D272].
The 5.2pp drop in FY2024 [D270] followed lower storm cost recovery of about $1.09 billion and fuel recovery down about $526 million [P34].
Operating income rose 10.7% in FY2025 [D237] against revenue growth of 9.8% [D236], an incremental margin of 34.8% [D256].
Diluted EPS fell 2.1% [D240] against a 1.6% fall in net income [D238], as diluted shares rose 0.6% [D251].
Operating margin of 32.1% [F24] is above its window median of 30.3% [D300] and the utilities peer median of 25.7% [D311].
Net margin of 26.5% [F40] sits 5.6pp below operating margin of 32.1% [F24], after net margin fell 3.1pp [D248].
The -17.7% effective tax rate [D226] reflects clean energy tax credits that rose about $585 million [P11].
Other income and expense widened from -$1.44 billion [X63] to -$3.75 billion [X64]; the filing cites about $1.00 billion of after-tax hedge losses [P8].
D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue from 23.2% [D224][D189], mainly on storm cost amortization of about $1.09 billion [P16].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion [F64] was 1.83x net income [D227], down from 1.91x in FY2024 [D192].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% [D241], partly because the shift to net under-recovery of clause costs reduced it by about $89 million [P19].
Capex is not in the pack, so free cash flow cannot be computed; D&A was 25.5% of revenue [D224].
Net debt of $92.2 billion [D231] is -357.4% of revenue [D232], the lowest of four peers [D314] against a median of -228.4% [D315].
Total debt reached $95.0 billion, up 15.7% [D230][D253], with $23.4 billion of debt issued [X90].
The current ratio of 0.60x [F128] is below 1.0x but above its window median of 0.52x [D306].
Dividends of $4.7 billion [X82] equalled 37.5% of operating cash flow [X82][F64].
Medium: net cash has fallen seven straight years, to -$92.2 billion [R2][D231].
The filings tie the FY2025 Corporate and Other drop to higher average debt and hedge losses [P8], pointing to financing cost rather than operations [P25].
Benign: revenue fell 5.2% in FY2024 [D201] on pass-through storm and fuel recovery [P34], and grew 9.8% in FY2025 [D236].
Data quality: the FY2020 share count rose 305.5% [D76] on the stock split [P74], so pre-FY2020 per-share figures are not directly comparable [X68][X69].
Operating margin should hold above its 30.3% window median [D300] from 32.1% [F24]; a drop below 30.3% [D300] would reverse the recovery in the FY2026 10-K.
Net debt at -357.4% of revenue [D232] is the trend to watch: further widening confirms it, and narrowing toward -228.4% [D315] reverses it, in the FY2026 10-K.
A tax rate back above FY2024's 5.6% [D191] would show the FY2025 benefit fading and push net margin below 26.5% [F40] in the FY2026 10-K.
